edits.find: Age >50 + bilateral proximal girdle aching with morning stiffness + systemic symptoms + ESR ≥50, with no true weakness and no muscle tenderness. edits.find: On the exam, PT is not wrong — it's not initial when the patient is still throwing every weekend. In clinic, modern tendinopathy management is relative rest plus progressive loading, and the two aren't really opposed. What matters at the bedside: say the words "do not wear a sling." Patients hear "rest" and immobilize, and the shoulder is uniquely punished for immobilization — adhesive capsulitis can set in within weeks.

edits.find: The LFCN is purely sensory — compressed under the inguinal ligament near the ASIS. No motor fibers means no weakness is possible, so 5/5 strength is confirmatory, not reassuring incidental data. Clinical diagnosis; conservative management resolves >90%.
edits.with: The LFCN (lateral femoral cutaneous nerve) is purely sensory. It is compressed under the inguinal ligament near the ASIS (anterior superior iliac spine). With no motor fibers, no weakness is possible, so 5/5 strength is confirmatory, not reassuring incidental data. Meralgia paresthetica is a clinical diagnosis. Conservative management resolves >90% of cases.
